answer: Approximately 24% (≈24%, 95% CI −8% to 67%): per additional ongoing medical condition (MHONGO='Yes'), the proportional-odds (cumulative-logit) ordinal regression predicts a 100×(exp(0.2152)−1) ≈ 24% increase in the odds of higher COVID-19 severity, controlling for BCG vaccination status (TRTGRP) and the patient-interaction variables (patients_seen, expect_interact). The effect is positive but not statistically significant in the primary analysis set (n=151 COVID-19 subjects with known severity; p≈0.16). Pre-specified sensitivities: (a) all 194 COVID subjects with unknown severity imputed at the lowest level → β=0.2005 (SE 0.1288, CI −0.052 to 0.453) ≈ 22% increase; (b) full cohort (n=1000, no COVID AE as lowest category 0) → β=0.2775 (SE 0.0727, CI 0.135–0.420) ≈ 32% increase, statistically significant; (c) covariate-expanded model adding Age/SEX/RACE/education/work_hours → β=0.2202 (SE 0.1731, CI −0.119 to 0.560) ≈ 25% increase. Binary any-ongoing sensitivity: β=0.5845 (SE 0.3387) ≈ 79% increase, not significant. Proportional-odds check: threshold-specific MHONGO coefficients are −0.02 (>1), 0.80 (>2), 0.83 (>3) in the primary set, i.e., the effect concentrates at the severe end; the common (proportional-odds) estimate of ~0.215 lies between them, but with only 18 events above level 2 and 7 above level 3 the assumption cannot be reliably verified and the ~24% figure should be read with that caveat.
